# Provenance

Every constant in `data/constants.js`, grouped by source.
`npm run provenance` rewrites this file after it checks that each constant
has a ref and a known source tag (`wowf-export`, `wowf-designer`,
`classic-1.12`, `cataclysm`, `assumption`, `engineering`). A missing ref,
a ref made only of dashes (including an em dash), a placeholder ref,
or an unknown tag fails the command. The check case-folds the ref.
Dashes, underscores, colons, slashes, backslashes, and bars separate
words. Other punctuation and symbols are deleted, and whitespace is
collapsed. `TBD`, `TBD.`, `TBD:x`, `TBD/James`, `N/A`, `NA`, `?`, `??`,
`tbd later`, `tbd-later`, `tbd_later`, and `fill_in` fail, as does a ref
made only of punctuation or symbols, or one whose first word is `tbd`.
The phrases `fill in` and `No recorded owner decision` fail only as
whole words.

## Summary

103 constants: 21 `wowf-export`, 5 `wowf-designer`, 40 `classic-1.12`, 1 `cataclysm`, 20 `assumption`, 16 `engineering`.

## engineering

16 constants. Simulator machinery, not a game rule. The retune flag stays off, so these rows are not on the retune list.

| id                           | value                                                                                                                                       | unit                     | ref                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | note                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | retune |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| `attack.rollScale`           | `100`                                                                                                                                       | roll                     | James, 22 Oct 2026: injected attack rolls use a 0–100 scale so tests can hit each boundary                                                                                                                                            | Not a game rule. Callers and the resolver tests depend on it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | no     |
| `rng.defaultSeed`            | `1`                                                                                                                                         | seed                     | James, 25 Oct 2026, issue #71: a Simulation built without a seed or an rng starts from this seed, so a bare run is repeatable                                                                                                         | Not a game rule. Any 32-bit integer is a valid seed. The live page picks its own seed at load.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | no     |
| `rng.mulberry32`             | `{ "increment": 1831565813, "shiftA": 15, "shiftB": 7, "mixOr": 61, "shiftC": 14, "range": 4294967296 }`                                    | mulberry32 terms         | James, 25 Oct 2026, issue #71: the published mulberry32 32-bit generator, so a seed gives the same sequence on every Node version and in the browser                                                                                  | Not a game rule. The Weyl increment, the three xor-shift widths, the second multiplier's OR term, and the 2^32 divisor that maps the 32-bit result into [0, 1). Changing any of them changes every seeded fight.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | no     |
| `config.weaponTypes`         | `[ "dagger", "sword", "mace", "axe", "fist", "other" ]`                                                                                     | weapon types             | James, 26 Oct 2026, issue #92: the weapon types a SimConfig accepts                                                                                                                                                                   | Not a game rule. Only "dagger" changes the engine today (the Ghostly Strike and Hemorrhage weapon percent, see weaponMultiplier). The others are accepted so talents and procs that name a weapon type (Hack and Slash, the sword and mace specialisations) have somewhere to read it from; "other" is the sample main hand. A hand may also have no type (null).                                                                                                                                                                    | no     |
| `config.poisonIds`           | `[ "instant", "deadly", "wound", "crippling", "mind-numbing" ]`                                                                             | poison ids               | James, 26 Oct 2026, issue #92: the poisons a SimConfig accepts on a weapon                                                                                                                                                            | Not a game rule. The five rogue poisons in the snapshot's spellbook. A SimConfig only stores the choice; no poison is simulated until A5. D9 (poison definitions from the snapshot) may replace this list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | no     |
| `config.minWeaponSpeed`      | `0.1`                                                                                                                                       | s                        | Developer, 26 Oct 2026, issue #93: an engineering judgement call by the dev, not a decision by James. The shortest swing time a SimConfig weapon (and a Weapon) may have, because the #111 QA found a 1e-9 s speed made runFight hang | Not a game rule. A weapon swings once per speed / haste seconds, and a swing of a billionth of a second means a billion swings a second, so the fight never finishes. 0.1 s is far below any real weapon (the sample weapons are 1.7 s and 1.8 s) and above sim.fixedStep, so one step never holds more than a handful of swings even with haste. Raise or lower it here if a test bench needs it.                                                                                                                                   | no     |
| `abilities.tabs`             | `[ "Assassination", "Combat", "Subtlety" ]`                                                                                                 | spellbook tabs           | James, 26 Oct 2026, issue #93: the spellbook tabs js/abilities.js builds abilities from                                                                                                                                               | Not a game rule. The snapshot's spellbook has these three class tabs, a Poisons tab and a hand-kept General list (Attack, Pick Lock, passives such as Dodge). Poisons are defined by D9 and the General list holds no rogue ability the simulator models, so neither is parsed here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | no     |
| `abilities.resources`        | `[ "energy" ]`                                                                                                                              | resource names           | James, 26 Oct 2026, issue #93: the resources a spell_desc cost cell may name ("45 Energy"), lower case                                                                                                                                | Not a game rule. Every cost cell in the Assassination, Combat and Subtlety tabs reads "N Energy". A cell like "45 sec" has the same shape but is a time, so js/abilities.js reads only the units listed here as costs and rejects the rest. Add a resource here when a class that spends it is parsed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | no     |

| `abilities.apCoefficients`   | `{ "eviscerate": { "kind": "perCp", "constant": "eviscerate.apPerCP" }, "rupture": { "kind": "totalByCp", "constant": "rupture.apByCP" } }` | ability id → constant id | James, 26 Oct 2026, issue #93: which constant holds each ability's AP coefficient                                                                                                                                                     | Not a game rule: a pointer, so the number is not written twice. The tooltip says Eviscerate, Rupture and Garrote are "increased by Attack Power" but gives no coefficient, so js/abilities.js reads it from the constant named here (with its own provenance). Eviscerate adds AP × CP × the constant. Rupture adds AP × the constant for the combo points spent, as a total over the whole DoT. Garrote has no coefficient yet, so its catalogue entry has ap: null until a constant exists.                                        | no     |

| `sim.maxFrameTime`           | `0.25`                                                                                                                                      | s                        | James, 25 Oct 2026, issue #76: the most wall-clock time one animation frame may feed the fight, so a hidden tab or a long pause cannot run it forward by the time it missed                                                           | Not a game rule. The live page takes at most 0.25 s of an animation frame (sim.maxFrameTime / sim.fixedStep steps, 16 at these values) and drops the rest, so a frame that arrives seconds late, as the first frame after a backgrounded tab does, advances the fight by 0.25 s and no more. At 60 fps a frame is about one step, so the cap never acts in normal use; it only starts to slow the fight below 4 frames per second.                                                                                                   | no     |
| `sim.msPerSecond`            | `1000`                                                                                                                                      | ms/s                     | James, 22 Oct 2026: the performance clock converts milliseconds to seconds                                                                                                                                                            | Unit conversion, not a game rule.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | no     |
| `sim.fixedStep`              | `0.015625`                                                                                                                                  | s                        | James, 25 Oct 2026, issue #73: the one time step every headless run uses, so a seed gives one fight                                                                                                                                   | Not a game rule. 1/64 s, close to a 60 fps frame and well below every game timer (GCD, swing speeds, DoT tick interval), so sim.tickEpsilon, swing timers and the GCD act as they do at live frame rates. It is a power of two, so adding it up is exact in floating point, a duration that is a whole number of steps lands on exactly that time, and a split at a step boundary reproduces the same fight. Results depend on the step size: changing it changes every seeded fight (the average DPS over many seeds barely moves). | no     |
